| R-02 | Major | aidlc/spaces/default/intents/260825-inventory-api/construction/inventory-api/infrastructure-design/monitoring-design.md > Alerts > Elevated 5xx, and SLIs / SLOs > Availability | The only alarm that can page, and the 99.9% availability SLI, are both worked out from the service's own log line (`statusCode`, `outcome=InternalError`). | R-03 | Major | aidlc/spaces/default/intents/260825-inventory-api/construction/inventory-api/infrastructure-design/infrastructure-specification.md > Infrastructure Services > DynamoDB table `Item` (failed-condition handling); traceability.json NFR1.2 | Upstream performance-design.md (Bounded retry row) says to retry internally on a conditional-check failure, treating it as transient contention. This design says that on a failed condition the repository reads the item once to tell ItemNotFound from InsufficientStock from overflow. The two contradict each other, and nothing here says which errors the ≤3 retry in NFR1.2 actually covers. With `SET quantity = quantity + :delta`, a failed condition is never contention: DynamoDB applies single-item updates one at a time. The follow-up read also races: if a concurrent increment lands between the failed update and the read, the read shows a state that would pass, and the design does not say what happens next. On the path the team calls its most important, a developer has to guess. | State that on ConditionalCheckFailedException the repository classifies and does not retry. Use `ReturnValuesOnConditionCheckFailure: ALL_OLD` on the UpdateItem so the item as it was at the failed check comes back with the error, with no second read and no race. Say what the bounded retry covers: throttling or internal-server errors only, beyond the AWS SDK's own default retries. Update the NFR1.2 target to match. | Resolved (reviewer) |
| R-04 | Minor | aidlc/spaces/default/intents/260825-inventory-api/construction/inventory-api/infrastructure-design/infrastructure-specification.md > DynamoDB table `Item` Notes ("No secondary indexes at MVP; every access is by sku") and IAM execution role row; traceability.json NFR1.4, NFR1.9 | WF3 in functional-spec.md lists all items with `limit`, `offset` up to 10000, and a `total` count. On a table whose only key is `sku`, with no secondary index, a DynamoDB Query needs an equality condition on one `sku`, so it cannot list across items. The design's "DynamoDB Query with Limit (≤100) serving bounded pagination" cannot be built as written. DynamoDB also has no offset: serving offset 10000 means reading and discarding 10000+ items, and `total` means counting the whole table. That makes the OK claims for NFR1.9 ("per-request work bounded independent of total item count") and NFR1.4 false, and contradicts performance-design.md's "no unbounded scans". The IAM row also lists Query as the list permission and leaves out Scan. | Pick and document the list access pattern. One option is a Scan with Limit plus a stated item-count ceiling for the MVP. Another is a GSI on a constant partition key with `sku` as sort key, or a maintained counter item for `total`. Say how `offset` and `total` are served and what they cost. Mark NFR1.9 as a known limit (or N/A with a ceiling) instead of OK if work grows with offset and table size. Fix the IAM action list to match. | Unresolved |

> R-01 Reviewer note: `GET /v1/health` is now its own route with no authorizer, beside `ANY /v1/{proxy+}` with the JWT authorizer. HTTP API picks the most specific route, so the open health route wins. The smoke test (cicd stage 13) and the canary both call `/v1/health`.

> R-02 Reviewer note: The 5xx alarm and the availability SLI now use API Gateway `5xx` / `Count`, and the doc says plainly that these cover timeouts, crashes, throttles and integration failures. The service log is kept for finding the cause only.

> R-03 Reviewer note: The DynamoDB row now says how a failed condition is classified (ALL_OLD from `ReturnValuesOnConditionCheckFailure`: no item, below min, above max), with no second read and no retry. Retries cover transient SDK errors only. The doc says openly where this narrows performance-design.

> R-04 Reviewer note: Fixed in substance: listing is a `Scan` with Limit and ExclusiveStartKey, the offset cap and the cost of the `total` count are stated, and NFR1.9 is now honestly `Deferred`. What is left: the IAM row says the role gets `GetItem/PutItem/UpdateItem/DeleteItem/Scan` "via CDK `table.grantReadWriteData(fn)`". That grant actually gives more: it also includes BatchGetItem, BatchWriteItem, Query, ConditionCheckItem, DescribeTable, GetRecords and GetShardIterator. Either use an explicit grant with only the five actions, or state the full action set the grant gives.

> R-05 Reviewer note: A CloudWatch Synthetics canary runs on `GET /v1/health` every 5 minutes. NFR1.13 and NFR3.1 are reworded, and the doc says API Gateway does no health checks on a Lambda integration.

> R-06 Reviewer note: The Lambda row now says on-demand per-request scaling with reserved concurrency 50 as the cap, and that target tracking applies only to provisioned concurrency.

> R-07 Reviewer note: A `live` alias is added and the API integrates `LambdaProxy(live)`. Rollback repoints the alias.

> R-08 Reviewer note: `deletionProtection: true` is in the snippet. A CDK `Table` defaults to the RETAIN removal policy. The Cognito pool also has deletion protection on.

> R-09 Reviewer note: The Cognito row now has `admin-set-user-password --permanent`.

> R-10 Reviewer note: Stage 10 now fails on unsuppressed Errors, with justified COG2 and COG3 suppressions written in code. One more gap is a new finding below.

> R-11 Reviewer note: `upstream_ids` and `coverage` hold the same 32 NFR ids, equal to the set in the nfr-design documents. `reverse` is empty.

### Summary

All four Major findings from iteration 1 are fixed: the health route, API Gateway-based 5xx and availability, classification of failed conditions, and the list access pattern with an honest NFR1.9. Traceability now fully covers all 32 NFR ids. What remains are Minor implementability gaps: request-id correlation, a repeatable smoke test, predictable cdk-nag suppressions, ownership of the canary's resources, a Lambda concurrency quota precondition, the retry and timeout budget, and the IAM grant wording. None of them blocks building this design.
